heroHeadline: Sudan Presses UN Security Council on UAE-Ethiopia Drone Attacks as Khartoum Airport Closure Enters Day 3
heroSubtitle: Khartoum International Airport remained closed on May 7 (Day 1118), with Sudan's Foreign Ministry advancing its evidence package — drone serial numbers, radar tracks, and wreckage — at the UN Security Council following last week's RSF/UAE loitering munition intercept over the airfield. Ambassador El Zain Ibrahim Hussein remained recalled from Addis Ababa as Sudan's diplomatic confrontation with Ethiopia escalated. The RSF's near-daily drone campaign continued across six theaters simultaneously (Khartoum corridor, White Nile State, North Kordofan, Blue Nile, Gezira, and Sennar), with UN OCHA warning that attacks on fuel and medical infrastructure are creating secondary humanitarian crises in SAF-controlled areas. An RSF drone strike on May 5 killed 5 civilians at fuel stations in Kosti, compounding the growing economic toll. Approximately 700+ civilians died in drone strikes in Q1 2026 alone, and 34 million people — 65% of Sudan's population — remain in urgent need of humanitarian support. The UAE continued to deny involvement in the airport attack, with an unnamed official questioning whether Port Sudan's government represents 'the legitimate government of Sudan.'
